findings.evidence: Hint: 'The endless ocean takes the whole push back of the move, the other way: the momentum of what they set moving or stop, plus whatever resists it while they push (a pulled load's rolling, a shoved partner's feet).' The engine (decision 3, throwOnce/tossPartner) sends only the object's momentum to the source and leaves the weight on his feet. Partner toss, 10 m lob, default dial, powers on: recoilAbsorbedT.J = 42,043 kg·m/s over a 0.348 s push. Ollie's weight resists the toss throughout, so the push back on Rex's arms is 42,043 + 3,000 × 9.81 × 0.348 = 42,043 + 10,238 = 52,281 kg·m/s. By the hint's rule the ocean would take 52,281; it takes 42,043 (20% less). The page itself says, rightly, 'The ground under him carries only his own weight and Ollie's.' The hard toss loses 8% the same way (62,404 vs 5,559). Default car throw at 45° (22,100 kg-force, real-muscle basis): push.t 0.247 s, mB 1,472 kg. The push back along the line, net of the arm's return, is 22,021 + 1,472 × 9.81 × sin 45° × 0.247 = 22,021 + 2,517 = 24,538; recoilAbsorbed.J = 22,021. So 'that push goes into their source: 22,000 kg·m/s' is 10% short of 'that push'.

The hint states the general rule without that exception, so it gives the wrong figure for any upward throw or toss.

The weight of what they hold up stays on their feet, as on the Lift tab.' Throw item: '...and the part of that push that moves the car goes into their source, the endless ocean: 22,000 kg·m/s, the car's momentum (its weight rests on his feet)'. No engine change.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced. The engine follows decision 3: with the power on, the source gets only the momentum of what is thrown (recoilAbsorbed.J = pObj), and his feet carry the weights (Nfeet = (body.m + obj.m) g). That decision is justified: holding a load up is weight, not recoil, as on the Lift tab, and the ledger closes. But two texts state a rule that includes the weight. The #sw-recoil hint (app.html L344) says the ocean takes 'the whole push back of the move ... the momentum of what they set moving or stop, plus whatever resists it while they push'. Gravity resists an upward throw or toss exactly as rolling resistance resists a pull, and for the pull the engine does put the resistance in the ocean. The Throw item (L1561) says 'the car pushes back on Rex exactly as hard as he pushes it, and that push goes into their source ...: 22,000 kg·m/s, the car’s momentum'. At 45° the push back from the car along the throw line over the push is the car's momentum plus the car's weight component times the push time: 22,020 + 2,292 = 24,312, so 'that push' is about 10% more than the figure. The finding's 2,517 includes the arm's own weight, which is internal to Rex. The car's own share is 2,292 (10.4%). For the partner toss the gap is larger: the easy lob takes 42,043 against 52,281 (20%), the hard toss 62,404 against 67,962 (8%). The toss text itself states the exception ('The ground under him carries only his own weight and Ollie’s'). The throw tab states it only when sinkRatioRaw > 1 (feetDown), so at the default car throw nothing tells the reader that the weight stays on his feet. A level throw is exact (RB = 0). The figure is labelled correctly as the car's momentum. The defect is the wording of the general rule and of 'that push', not the engine.
